fatal_errors: The cited evidence only demonstrates the nanoflake coating on steel at approximately 20–25 °C in ambient humidity; it does not support performance on CoCrFeNi or at temperatures approaching 800 °C.
The prediction of a coefficient of friction near 0.08–0.1 and an order-of-magnitude wear reduction throughout 25–800 °C is an unjustified extrapolation from room-temperature results.
High-temperature oxidation, sulfur loss, coating/substrate reactions, and thermal-expansion mismatch are not addressed, even though they could destroy a dichalcogenide coating well below 800 °C.

Evidence E4 reports rapid failure and substantially higher wear when the coating solvent is changed, directly contradicting the claim of robust performance across environmental conditions; this conflict is not acknowledged.
The intervention is not strictly singular because it combines the nanoflake coating with an adhesion-promoting interlayer or an unspecified post-deposition heat treatment.

The falsification rule is too permissive: a claim of consistent performance over the full range should be falsified by failure at any prespecified temperature, load, or environment, rather than only by failure across the entire set.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad wide-temperature friction-and-wear problem and proposes a novel coating with measurable outcomes, but it does not reconstruct the target intervention of varying Mo content in an SPS-fabricated CoCrFeNiMox–Ni/MoS2–Ag–Cr2O3 composite. Its mechanism also differs from the target's Mo solid-solution and sigma-phase strengthening combined with temperature-dependent MoS2/Ag lubrication and high-temperature silver-molybdate glaze formation. Most importantly, the supporting study establishes low friction only for a steel tribopair at room temperature. It provides no evidence that the coating remains chemically or mechanically stable on CoCrFeNi at 200–800 °C. The baseline is qualitative, operating conditions omit key controlled quantities such as counterface, speed, and distance, and the claimed environmental robustness conflicts with the cited water-processing failure. The proposed experiment could test the idea, but it needs prespecified temperature/load/environment cells, an uncoated control under identical conditions, and a falsification criterion triggered by failure in any required cell.
